name: elementor
notes: The admitted line is Elementor 4.x ([4.0.0, 5.0.0)). Exact official WordPress.org 4.0.0 and 4.2.3 artifacts are the certified boundaries, 4.0.0 -> 4.2.3 is exercised in place, and the real 3.35.9 release is the adjacent refusal control. Elementor Pro, third-party add-ons, multisite, e-floating-buttons entities, global classes/variables/components, and other extension-owned entity stores remain outside this free-plugin contract until separately inventoried and tested.

_elementor_data is Elementor's own postmeta rendering source (verified empirically: post_content is a plain-HTML fallback used by feeds/search/non-JS contexts, NOT what the front-end renders) — a JSON blob wp_json_encode()'d WITHOUT JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES, so every '/' in it appears as '\/'. Classified authored with json_encoded + json_refs: the raw string is JSON-decoded, declared paths rewrite ids through the ledger, every OTHER string leaf (the redundant 'url' sibling on every media control, arbitrary link/text content) is tokenize_text()'d automatically, and the whole rewritten structure is stored NATIVELY (nested, not re-stringified) in the captured state/ tree — far more readable/mergeable than one opaque minified blob, and the escaping is regenerated for free on apply's re-encode (Tokens::tokenize_text()/detokenize_text() are escaped-form-aware now; RFC 8259 makes '/' vs '\/' interchangeable inside a JSON string, so this is lossless).

The classic editor media shapes were produced through Document::save(): image, background_image, and wp_gallery store {id,url} records under arbitrarily nested elements. Elementor 4.2.3's active Atomic Image widget uses a distinct generated prop envelope, image.value.src.value.id.value, and that exact path is independently seeded/rendered. Plain URL links carry no WordPress id and rebind through the structured value's recursive string tokenizer.

The loud-gate keys, precise and reproduced independently twice (original report + this session's own fx1/fx2 probes): activation + a builder save surfaces seven keys (_elementor_data/_elementor_edit_mode/_elementor_template_type authored; _elementor_version managed; _elementor_page_assets/_elementor_global_class_usage_indexed/_elementor_global_class_usage_indexed_preview derived). A REAL front-end page visit (confirmed again this session via curl, not just wp-cli flush-css) lazily creates three MORE: _elementor_css/_elementor_element_cache derived, and a versioned _elementor_migrations_state_<hash> key handled by meta_patterns below since the hash suffix is not a stable literal (differs per Elementor release/site) — Policy::rule() previously had no post_meta/term_meta pattern-fallback at all; meta_patterns (mirroring the existing option_patterns) closes that gap. A conformance seed for this manifest MUST include a render step (front-end page visit) before its second capture or it will falsely believe the manifest is complete — the original report's own finding, reproduced.

elementor_active_kit is a post reference into the declared elementor_library type. Elementor 4.2.3's Kit::update_settings() persists global colors, typography, responsive/site settings, and media controls as native PHP plain data in _elementor_page_settings. The manifest owns that full authored value, tokenizes all strings, and rewrites the exact site_logo, site_favicon, background_image, and background_slideshow_gallery attachment shapes exercised by the live estate.

Rebuilder verified against a running install (task #11 wave 2): Elementor ships `wp elementor flush-css` (module: modules/wp-cli/command.php, alias flush-css) with a --regenerate flag that clears the CSS cache and calls Plugin::$instance->files_manager->generate_css() — confirmed by reading the installed plugin's own source (not assumed from memory) and running it live (`wp elementor flush-css --regenerate` -> "Success: Flushed the Elementor CSS Cache"). This is what turns correctly-rewritten _elementor_data into a rendered page: Elementor's CSS (including section background-image URLs, which live in generated CSS, not in any HTML attribute) is compiled from _elementor_data at cache-generation time, so it picks up the target environment's own rewritten ids/URLs automatically — confirmed by rendering a genuinely cross-environment-applied page and finding the section background-image in the regenerated CSS file already pointing at the target's own host.

elementor-css provider 2.0.0 preflights the core post/postmeta schema before Elementor's destructive clear-cache command, requires a typed warning-free native WP-CLI receipt, clears rendered HTML/page-asset caches, hashes generated file contents, and verifies a closed published-builder-document to post-<id>.css relation with no missing or orphan files. The action is trigger-bounded and records restorable options/postmeta checkpoints plus the regenerable uploads/elementor/css filesystem effect.

post_types.elementor_library (Elementor 4.2.3 exact live adoption): declared structurally because Elementor's custom active kit and saved templates live in this non-public post type. elementor_active_kit is a ref:post into that scope; omitting the type makes init/capture refuse unresolved_option_reference_scope instead of silently retaining an environment-local kit id.
